Legs.Subject: TryFactorize over QuadraticAlgebra<BigInteger> succeeds with zero obstructions across the nine imaginary class-number-one worlds (Delta = -3, -4, -7, -8, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163) and the real Delta = 5 world, swept by a deterministic arithmetic-progression element stream (no System.Random) rather than at one hand-picked value; each world's Discriminant is checked against its expected value before anything else runs

every returned prime factor is re-checked twice over: IsPrimeElement confirms it is genuinely prime, and CanonicalAssociate is IDEMPOTENT on it (CanonicalAssociate(factor.Prime) == factor.Prime), so a factorization that produced a composite or a non-canonical representative would fail here even though it never reaches a reassembly mismatch

the leading unit times each canonical prime power, multiplied back through the algebra's own Multiply, reproduces the input element exactly, and the leading factor is independently confirmed a unit by IsUnit rather than merely assumed from its role

ENVELOPE: reassembly composes QuadraticAlgebra<BigInteger>.Multiply and Conjugate/Negate reach through CanonicalAssociate's unit-orbit search, so this case does not isolate any one of those from TryFactorize's own arithmetic; Multiply is independently pinned over the FixedQ4816 carrier by algebra.complex-lane-vs-oracle and its neighbours, and here it is exercised only as the composition the factorization contract itself promises to close

at the descriptor (P, Q) = (1, 1), FundamentalUnit returns exactly (0, 1) — the adjoined root x itself, which IS phi by construction (x^2 = x + 1). A hand computation of the SAME norm formula the type implements gives Norm(0,1) = 0^2 + 1*0*1 - 1*1^2 = -1, which is a definitional fact about this descriptor checked directly rather than a value captured from running the subject and fed back to it
SplittingCharacter at Delta = 5 over every prime below 2000
Legs.Against: a binary quadratic-reciprocity descent (RefJacobiSymbol) written fresh in QuadraticIntegerClaims.cs, sharing no line with NumberTheoryFunctions.JacobiSymbol or UnsignedNumberFunctions.JacobiSymbol, either of which SplittingCharacter itself could reach; 2 is decided by Delta mod 8 independently on both sides, and an odd prime by the reciprocity symbol against 5 versus the residue test ell mod 5 == 0 for the ramified case

Legs.Subject: SplittingCharacter agrees with the norm-ell factor test on the SAME rational prime: the character is anything but Inert exactly when a norm-ell prime element was found, tying two different subject calls together rather than checking either alone

Legs.Subject: at Delta = -19, calling TryFactorize twice on each of a hundred deterministic elements returns byte-identical factorizations (same leading unit, same prime powers in the same order) or byte-identical obstructions, at every one of them

Norm, IsUnit and IsPrimeElement across four worlds (three class-number-one, one non-principal) and three routing regimes — comfortably inside the 2^41 fixed-width fast-tier bound, straddling it, and comfortably above it

Legs.Subject: IsPrimeElement's inert-square branch — a norm equal to the square of an INERT rational prime — is driven EXPLICITLY through algebra.Root rather than left to chance (random components almost never land a norm exactly ell^2), and judged consistently by IsPrimeElement, by the CanonicalAssociate-based associate comparison, and by the independent reference alike

Legs.Subject: every delegated answer satisfies X^2 - D*Y^2 = 1 exactly, checked independently of the transcription comparison above

at D = 991 (Delta = 3964, the exact input the audit found FundamentalUnit hanging on) and D = 99991 (Delta = 399964), both radicands D are checked LIVE to be 3 (mod 4) — not Delta = 4*D, which is always 0 (mod 4) and would trip on nothing — and then it is checked EXHAUSTIVELY over every (x, y) in [0, 4) x [0, 4) that no residue makes x^2-D*y^2 congruent to -1 (mod 4). Since Certificate = X^2-Delta*Y^2 = 4*(a^2-D*b^2) = 4*Norm(unit) for a (0, D) descriptor, this is the FORCED-sign argument for Norm itself, verified rather than assumed, which is why the returned unit's Norm is required to be exactly +1 and not merely +-1

FundamentalUnit completes inside a bounded wait (a safety net against a regression of the former hang, not a timing measurement — the assertion is completion, never elapsed time) at both discriminants, each producing a certificate X^2-Delta*Y^2 = +-4

at both discriminants, neither X+2 nor X-2 is a perfect square, which rules out the returned unit being some other unit's own square (an index-two answer) — minimality itself rests on the period argument FundamentalUnit's own continued-fraction walk performs, not on this check
